title: a nested drain hands each envelope over once
intention: BaseShim._check_mail drains from a snapshot of undelivered mail. When a handler asks and the bus server drains the same mailbox again from inside the wait (_serve_held), the inner drain takes the rest of the snapshot and the outer loop then hands each of those envelopes over a second time. A shim now remembers what any drain in the current batch has taken and the outer loop skips it.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 03:09:50-51 UTC in ~/.cairn/logs/bus/0: asks 4b518544, 80b9e419 and 609d25fb (CC to codemother, posted 02:58-03:05, CC gave up on each) were delivered to codemother 2, 3 and 2 times in 1.7 s. The first reply to each was receipted bus-asker-gave-up. The four replies after it (fb8242a2, 09a1f6b0, 90919898, 2d846154) have no branch in post() and stood, raising mail-cc-stood-600s 20 times.
traces_to: CLAUDE.md RULE 1; outline 5.8.3.3 (a shim processes all messages from the bus for its device); outline 17.13.1.
how: cairn/tools/base/shim.py: _check_mail counts its depth and calls _drain_mail (its old body). An envelope is added to _taken_in_drain once deliver() returns. The waiting list and each loop step skip ids in that set. The set clears when the outermost drain returns, so it never grows past one batch and later mail is still delivered. New proof proofs/test_a_nested_drain_takes_each_envelope_once.py.

clauses.claim: with three envelopes waiting and the first handler draining the mailbox from inside, each envelope reaches the device once and is receipted once
mail that arrives after the outer drain returns is still delivered by the next drain

decisions.text: D1: the shim skips what a drain in its current batch took; the server's serving of held shims stays.
